children: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries shares fell more than 2 percent in early trade on September 1, paring three-session gains after the drugmaker agreed to lower US drug prices in return for tariff concessions. Sun Pharma agreed to extend Most Favored Nation (MFN) pricing to US state Medicaid programmes and future innovative medicine launches as part of an agreement with the US government.

The stock fell 2.3 percent to Rs 1,940, making it one of the top losers on the Nifty 50. The decline came after a 3.4 percent gain in the previous session and snapped a three-day winning run during which the stock had risen about 4.5 percent. The broader market was also trading lower. At 9:17 am, the Sensex was down 83.64 points, or 0.11 percent, at 76,873.63, while the Nifty 50 fell 44.15 points, or 0.18 percent, to 24,036.25.

Sun Pharma said on Tuesday that it joined several pharmaceutical companies at a White House ceremony to announce agreements with the US government aimed at improving access to affordable medicines for American patients.

Under the agreement, Sun Pharma will extend MFN pricing to state Medicaid programmes and has also committed to MFN pricing for future innovative medicine launches. The remaining terms of the agreement are confidential.

The pricing commitments could potentially weigh on realisations from medicines covered by the agreement, although the financial impact cannot yet be quantified as Sun Pharma did not disclose details such as the products covered, applicable pricing benchmarks or the extent of its affected sales.

In return, the agreement provides Sun Pharma with a significant concession on the tariff front. The company said the US government has agreed to delay the application of Section 232 tariffs on its innovative pharmaceutical products for more than two years, recognising Sun Pharma's investments in the country.

The tariff reprieve assumes significance given the importance of the US to Sun Pharma's growth strategy. The US accounts for approximately 27 percent of the company's global revenue and is its largest market for innovative medicines.

Sun Pharma has progressively expanded beyond its traditional US generics business into higher-value innovative and specialty medicines. Its global innovative medicines portfolio, spanning dermatology, ophthalmology and onco-dermatology, now accounts for about 22 percent of company sales.
The company's exposure to the US is also set to increase following its definitive agreement earlier this year to acquire Organon & Co. at an enterprise value of $11.75 billion.

Despite Tuesday's decline, Sun Pharma shares have gained about 15 percent so far in 2026, substantially outperforming the Nifty 50, which is down nearly 8 percent over the same period. The drugmaker had a market capitalisation of more than Rs 4.76 lakh crore based on Monday's closing price.
